reviews.text: Brilliant acting but unless you enjoy alternative cinema this is not a film that you are going to enjoy. It is a slow slog.
reviews.author: David Griffiths

reviews.text: As the film unfolded, I felt like I was slowly going insane alongside the characters. My anxiety and confusion galvanised into the most immersive of experiences.
reviews.author: Calum Cooper

reviews.text: Shot on black and white 35mm film, Eggers’ feature never loses its mysterious yet vibrant atmosphere.
reviews.author: Brittany Patrice Witherspoon

reviews.text: Working in harmony, Mark Korven’s musical horror and Damien Volpe’s sound design consistently bubble under the surface, hinting at unsettling and unfolding motifs.
reviews.author: Tommy James

reviews.text: Filmed in beautiful black-and-white with a claustrophobic aspect ratio, Robert Eggers delivers a story about loneliness and isolation that takes the weirdest, craziest route. I don't have a single complaint, and I love it more the more I think about it.
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: As a dark fable, The Lighthouse resonates on the level of collective memory and myth, providing a thoroughly engrossing, veritable masterpiece of performance, period detail and visual inventiveness.
reviews.author: Paul Kanieski

reviews.text: ...you can almost taste the sea-salt and smell the stench of booze in the air. Robert Eggers’ “The Lighthouse” is a sea yarn full of sailor superstitions; it could be the most haunting film about sea-lore ever made. Save it for a cold stormy night.
reviews.author: Wael Khairy

reviews.text: a rich and strange sea yarn in monochrome that overflows with Beckettian absurdity, as these men, perhaps both liars (literal gaslighters), look, while waiting for ‘relief’, into the abyss of both their elemental isolation & their infernal companionship.
reviews.author: Anton Bitel

reviews.text: When you confine two people in a small space, there's not a lot of room for secrets, lust, fights, hallucinations, kinship or farts...over time, such confinement can make any sane man question reality...
reviews.author: Patrick Holland

reviews.text: It's a film that lingers in the corner of your mind as you find yourself wondering how the hell they shot certain parts, replaying monologues and drunken arguments in your head, resurfacing shots that perfectly pair the repulsive and beautiful.
reviews.author: Morgan Little

reviews.text: A comedy as black as the ocean floor, The Lighthouse will draw audiences in with its siren’s song and leave them breathless and broken against the rocks with images that will stay with you like the ships trapped in Davy Jones’s locker.
reviews.author: Dallas King

reviews.text: Eggers injects some unexpected levity into this seafaring genre tale, but it's Dafoe and Pattinson who carry the show.
reviews.author: Trace Thurman

reviews.text: I worked really hard to like this movie, overlooking my frustrations and pushing forward for something more than the beautiful B&W visuals and intensely committed performances. But I never found it...
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: …The Lighthouse is a cheeky provocation, cleverly made and making great use of two deservedly popular actors…
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: The images are between beautiful and overwhelming, and the performances, the counterpoints between Dafoe and Pattinson, whether or not they are drunk, supreme. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: Eggers has watched with interest the first films of Guy Maddin and surely also something by the Quay Brothers. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fernando E. Juan Lima

reviews.text: A stone-cold masterpiece.
reviews.author: Cole Smithey

reviews.text: Robert Eggers has established himself as cinema's premier researcher, capable of evoking a historical period with centuries-old vernaculars, period-accurate tactile details, and a visual schema rooted in the past.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: This psychological horror drama is jammed with nightmarish imagery and tour de force acting.
reviews.author: Steve Crum

reviews.text: Episode 52: Jojo Rabbit / The Lighthouse / Parasite
reviews.author: Taylor Baker

reviews.text: An extraordinary, unsettling film that will stay with you long after the final credits.
reviews.author: Elizabeth Aubrey

reviews.text: The Lighthouse is a crazy hallucinogenic trip that is extremely original. The two actors' physiognomy is very well used. There are many unforgettable imageries. The Lighthouse is a quite unique movie watching experience.
reviews.author: Dustin Chang

reviews.text: An expertly rendered gothic slow burn that brings with it an atmosphere of dread which shrouds the film like fog rolling onto shore.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: It's likely you'll find few movies as simultaneously vulgar and literate as The Lighthouse.
reviews.author: Fletcher Powell

reviews.text: Amidst the dread, and dark humor, and bonkers imagery that makes The Lighthouse a weird little marvel, it's arguably Pattinson who really drives it home as a horror film.
reviews.author: Jesse Hassenger

reviews.text: It's all very weird, psychosexual, comical, surreal, maddening, and even nonsensical at times (merging a bit of Bunuel and Deren with Lynch and Jodorowsky).
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: Too artsy, too far fetched, and by the time we get to any reveals, well, I just don't care anymore. The only reason this gets a 1 out of 5 instead of 0 is the acting.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: The Lighthouse takes so long getting somewhere, and that destination is so murky, that you may well have stopped caring well before getting there.
reviews.author: Dennis Harvey

reviews.text: Easily one of 2019's most unique, original, and rewarding motion pictures.
reviews.author: Richard Propes

reviews.text: If you ever had a desire to be a lighthouse keeper, I guarantee you, Robert Eggers' The Lighthouse will make you re-think that profession!
reviews.author: Kelechi Ehenulo

reviews.text: As a storm rolls in, all hell breaks loose, pitting Thomas and Ephraim against one another. The final shot is a jaw-dropper that will have you chewing over the entrails of this cracking horror movie for years to come.
reviews.author: Stephen A. Russell

reviews.text: Eggers has, in the end, opportunistically produced a paean to present-day identity politics...
reviews.author: Joanne Laurier

reviews.text: This is new weird genre territory, and [Robert Eggers] has intentionally crafted a maximalist sensory experience.
reviews.author: Luke Gorham

reviews.text: Hitchcockian sexuality and Kalatozov-esque atmospherics aside, Robert Eggers is eager to plunge audiences into the fog.
reviews.author: Matt Cipolla

reviews.text: For all its powerful performances and haunting imagery, its setting is too bleak, its narrative too experimental, its director too indulgent, its purpose for existing too unclear.
reviews.author: Jason Fraley

reviews.text: The primal violence that often binds men has rarely been evoked as intensely ... [Dafoe and Pattinson's] pairing provides a recipe for one unforgettable moment after another as they drink, dance and dispute over everything, from supper to superstitions.
reviews.author: Prahlad Srihari

reviews.text: The pair strike a perfect tonal balance. Can a duo win Best Ensemble at the SAG awards? It would be well-deserved in this case.
reviews.author: Scott Phillips

reviews.text: Atmospheric it may be, but The Lighthouse is in other key respects very, very dull indeed.
reviews.author: Keri O'Shea

reviews.text: Dafoe is in full control of his craft, creating a performance for the ages. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ricardo Gallegos

reviews.text: It is a tense, concise and visually atmospheric film that manages to surprise me with the story of the two confined lighthouse keepers. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: It's a bleak, esoteric and mind-bending trip to the edges of insanity, wrapped in a sobering study of the effects of isolation.
reviews.author: Damond Fudge

reviews.text: "The Lighthouse" begs for an immediate rewatch to unravel, unpack, and decipher, and it's certainly the kind of film that benefits from multiple viewings. Whether it all coheres or not is a topic I'm sure will be debated, but it's a spectacle to behold.
reviews.author: Brent McKnight

reviews.text: The Lighthouse is a dense piece of cinema that's hard to pin down with a simple four paragraph review, and is only complicated by the film's overlapping tone colors and pitch-black, meme worthy humor.
reviews.author: Dan Tabor

reviews.text: It was interesting.
reviews.author: Avaryl Halley

reviews.text: Robert Eggers's sophomore effort takes us on a surreal down spiral tale, boosted by Pattinson and Daffoe's heart wrenching performances and some of the most disturbing imagery Horror has offered in the past couple of years.
reviews.author: Alejandro Turdó

reviews.text: The process of degradation is shown in a superficial manner. It's a narrative flaw. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: William Venegas

reviews.text: ...this is the cinematic equivalent of that seal throwing an octopus at a kayaker. I am the kayaker, the octopus is The Lighthouse, and Robert Eggers is the seal throwing it in my face saying, 'here, take this and enjoy it, you heathen'.
reviews.author: Andrew F. Peirce

reviews.text: Robert Eggers throws you headfirst into the deep end of the late 19th century with every period detail (and fart) intact.
reviews.author: Karl Delossantos

reviews.text: By the grace of Neptune, The Lighthouse is a must-see.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: One of the biggest stumbling blocks to appreciating this film is its constant attempts to defy expectations and avoid definitions.
reviews.author: Wesley Lovell

reviews.text: This movie was real weird... but we liked that.
reviews.author: Andrew Galdi

reviews.text: Without Pattinson and Dafoe's increasingly riotous bickering, the movie would collapse under its own storm, but sure enough, they steer it through.
reviews.author: Dan Schindel

reviews.text: The Lighthouse may be challenging, it may even be off-putting, but it's gutsy, accomplished and the kind of movie that sears into your memory.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: A disturbing study of traditional masculinity, a descent to madness and confusion, from the perspective of a character who can't always be trusted. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: The Lighthouse is a horror movie done just the way I like them.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: It's unsettling at times, yes, but also utterly mesmerising.
reviews.author: Toby Woollaston

reviews.text: The Lighthouse is, at its squirmy core, one of the most uniquely deranged buddy movies to come out in quite some time.
reviews.author: Aaron Yap

reviews.text: The film is a head-scratching, exhilarating and just damned bonkers work that is richly singular in execution.
reviews.author: Frank J. Avella

reviews.text: There's a bit of Hemingway in the way director Robert Eggers tells the tale of "The Lighthouse." From masculine relationships to the ability to weave old myths through new images, Eggers presents it all as a long-lost artifact.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: It illustrates its central conflict vividly, but a clearer allegory is lost in the deep mist.
reviews.author: Damien Straker

reviews.text: One for the ages...writer/director Robert Eggers' seductive, hallucinatory film is a brilliantly contrived cinematic tone poem...
reviews.author: Doris Toumarkine

reviews.text: The atmosphere is ugly, claustrophobic, hermetic, the images murky and relentless. There seems no doubt Eggers is an original and talented filmmaker, but he hasn't made it easy on the audience with this grim, forbidding movie.
reviews.author: David Stratton

reviews.text: The suspense and supernatural elements-especially as filmed in film-noir, 35-millimeter black-and-white-are as palpable as they are astonishing. A brilliant achievement.
reviews.author: Stephen Rebello

reviews.text: A gloriously bonkers two-hander.
reviews.author: Ed Whitfield

reviews.text: A mix of folklore, myth, & queer identity makes for perfectly dark fantasy crossed with horror, and the film's themes challenge 19th-century heteronormative narratives.
reviews.author: C.H. Newell

reviews.text: This is still at times pretty damn scary, but the uncanny mood keeps being dissipated by undeniable silliness and a certain fishy pretension.
reviews.author: David 'Mad Dog' Bradley

reviews.text: Eggers can't quite unlock the revelatory moments in this meld of high symbolism and psychological inquiry... While he's made a film that is brilliant in stretches, it remains emotionally distant.
reviews.author: Jason Di Rosso

reviews.text: There's plenty of fun to be had here, to be sure, but at a certain point it feels insufficiently unhinged to conjure the giddy seasickness to which it strives.
reviews.author: Luke Goodsell

reviews.text: Best appreciated by those who relish a cinematic challenge.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: From the opening shot there's never any doubt the director is in absolute control. Not just of every scene and every moment, but of every shadow and every stream of light
reviews.author: Luke Buckmaster

reviews.text: Shot in stark black & white in academy ratio, director Robert Eggers has an absolute ball creating havoc for these two souls, mixing surrealism into a playfully bleak horror scenario...its claustrophobic intensity and portrayal of madness are compelling.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: Wake In Fright meets Ida meets Splash.
reviews.author: CJ Johnson

reviews.text: Robert Pattinson and Willem Dafoe go hell for leather as deranged lighthouse keepers fighting their claustrophobic entrapment.
reviews.author: Andiee Paviour

reviews.text: As with The Witch, it's the atmosphere that seeps into you like sea brine. You don't watch this film, you are submerged in it. Expect to be spat out, reeling, from the cinema, clutching on to your sanity.
reviews.author: Larushka Ivan-Zadeh

reviews.text: American writer-director Robert Eggers excels at transporting you into the past and putting you under the skin of those you meet there. Persuading you to be glad that you came is another matter.
reviews.author: Sandra Hall

reviews.text: But what you really need to know about this exploration of madness, mermaids and marine isolation is that it's in black and white, shot in an old-fashioned upright ratio and not nearly as clever as it thinks it is.
reviews.author: Matthew Bond

reviews.text: Very much going to be deemed a masterpiece by some, and a muddling mess by others.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: While the desperate intensity of Willem Dafoe and Robert Pattinson's performances complements The Lighthouse's increasingly unhinged register, it's not enough to save the film.
reviews.author: Vicky Roach

reviews.text: From its distinctive look to Willem Dafoe getting a mouthful of dirt, this is one of the more memorable films of the year.
reviews.author: Matthew Toomey

reviews.text: The lewd, overwrought, Herman Melville-inspired dialogue is alternately mumbled and shouted, the intense, grand guignol performances more interesting as an experiment than conducive to eliciting meaning.
reviews.author: Simran Hans

reviews.text: A provocative planning that comes out brilliantly reinforced of every risk it assumes. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alberto Luchini

reviews.text: But despite the superb performances from both actors, cinematography that makes almost every frame look like an exquisitely lit monochrome photo, and conspicuous nods to Alfred Hitchcock, I didn't enjoy a single minute of their company.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: The Lighthouse is a pressure-cooker.
reviews.author: David Sexton

reviews.text: A piercing psychological horror.
reviews.author: Michael Lee

reviews.text: Surreal, confusing, funny and shocking, it does not entirely succeed. But there is more than enough here to merit a visit.
reviews.author: Jamie East

reviews.text: While Wick's penchant for standing naked before the lantern is admittedly odd, it's Winslow's dreams and hallucinations - and his violence towards the local seagulls, inviting bad luck - that fill the film with foreboding.
reviews.author: Demetrios Matheou

reviews.text: The end result is horrific and hilarious - and all the better for it.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: It's the kind of language that roots you to the spot, and it's terrific, much like everything else.
reviews.author: Deborah Ross

reviews.text: It is perfectly possible to admire the film and to still feel that it amounts to little more than a storm in a teacup. A painstakingly sourced authentic period teacup with original 19th-century patterning, of course, but a teacup all the same.
reviews.author: Ryan Gilbey

reviews.text: a barking study in madness
reviews.author: Chris Hunneysett

reviews.text: If you're up for some weird, dense, symbolist gear, then The Lighthouse might just be the beacon in the darkness you've been searching for.
reviews.author: Anthony O'Connor

reviews.text: What it lacks in overall coherence is made up for with a collection of brilliant individual contributions.
reviews.author: Tom Duggins

reviews.text: The longer the film goes on, the weirder it gets and the more it resembles a sitcom - The Odd Couple in sou'westers, a droll symphony of bodily functions, bubbling friction and all manner of desires that dare not speak their name.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: Eggers masters the dangerous mix of horror and comedy.
reviews.author: Elena Lazic

reviews.text: Plodding narrative aside, this study of how a lack of intimacy and boredom can manifest in insanity is a must-watch for arthouse cinema lovers.
reviews.author: Jasmine Lim

reviews.text: The Lighthouse is the sort of film that recognises the beauty of ugliness in nearly all its forms and turns it into beautiful monochrome imagery.
reviews.author: Steven Sheehan

reviews.text: A towering triumph.
reviews.author: Harry Guerin

reviews.text: A slow-burn descent into claustrophobic madness, 'The Lighthouse' is every bit as breathtaking as it is unsettling. It's that rare breed of film that can terrify as much as it can thrill.
reviews.author: Doug Jamieson

reviews.text: Conjuring menace and mystery from solitude and seagulls, The Lighthouse is a folk tale, a black comedy, a horror, a mystery, a (platonic?) romance - and something more still, something unspeakable. Something like a masterpiece, perhaps.
reviews.author: John Nugent

reviews.text: A dizzying blend of horror, dark comedy, tense psychological drama and fantasy that will keep you captivated.
reviews.author: Ian Sandwell

reviews.text: The mental deterioration of Wake and Winslow is impeccably executed, but the characters are so hard to stomach it's hard to care.
reviews.author: Jorge Ignacio Castillo

reviews.text: Unlikely as it seems, Dafoe and Pattinson have given us one of the oddest, craziest and tenderest on-screen couples of the year.
reviews.author: Kong Rithdee

reviews.text: "The Lighthouse" has echoes of Melville and Lovecraft as well as Coleridge and Greek mythology, all stirred together in a psychedelic stew, or a cup of turpentine and honey. The honey is the film's sumptuous aesthetic.
reviews.author: Rob Gonsalves

reviews.text: Ephraim Winslow (a never better Robert Pattinson) is a young man who takes a job as an assistant to an old lighthouse keeper, Thomas Wake (a haunting Willem Dafoe).
reviews.author: Mina Takla

reviews.text: An oppressive and fascinating maritime film. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: A beautiful extravagance that's weighed down by its excess. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Loser

reviews.text: A muddy, murky mess of a movie. I almost went crazy trying to figure out if the characters were crazy. Still Willem Dafoe can do no wrong when it comes to acting.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: The Lighthouse is an exceptional film that requires patience and openness from the conventional viewer. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fausto Ponce

reviews.text: As he demonstrated in The Witch, [Robert] Eggers is a very talented director. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jaime Fa de Lucas

reviews.text: Its fantastic, imposing, and esoteric images -- as beautiful as they are terrifying -- are in a league of their own. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Desirée De Fez

reviews.text: Watching The Lighthouse is like being stuck in a nightmare without understanding how nor why. [Full review in Portuguese]
reviews.author: Pablo Villaça

reviews.text: Pattinson and Dafoe are well matched and give outstanding performances. They play off each other like dueling pianos in a quest for dominance.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: An incredible, desperately weird, frightening masterpiece.
reviews.author: Brian Lloyd

reviews.text: The parable is instructive and its cinematographic expression... is here, at times, really overwhelming. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Bonfil

reviews.text: The Lighthouse is a splendid and unsettling movie that evokes the superiority and power of the sea. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Fernando Galván

reviews.text: A perfect combination of Lovecraftian elements and some of David Lynch's surrealist ideas. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Abigail Camarillo

reviews.text: The light, the wind, the food, the beds, and even the seagulls end up becoming something different, something unsettling... In the Lighthouse, it's easy to lose one's mind. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Quim Casas

reviews.text: Willem Dafoe and Robert Pattinson are wonderful in this beautifully shot, descent into madness. [Full in Spanish}
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: [Its] style-over-substance aesthetic seems to treat surrealism as just a simple horror technique rather than a psychological tool - and the result is eerie but feels somehow more shallow than The Witch.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: The film's visceral assault on the senses is helped by Willem Dafoe and Robert Pattinson who give stunning performances as the two leads.
reviews.author: Sean O'Rourke

reviews.text: [I]n The Lighthouse, Eggers engages us in a struggle for consciousness that is as ancient as it is essential.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: The Lighthouse can be enjoyed on dual levels - as a thickly atmospheric exercise in psychological terror, or as a compendium of seafaring legends, jokes and clichés.
reviews.author: Nathaniel Bell

reviews.text: ... refusal to commit to any revealing detail undoes the goodwill, leaving a thick atmosphere without tangible meaning while blaming "madness" for lacking cohesion.
reviews.author: Kevin A. Ranson

reviews.text: This movie will mess...you...up.
reviews.author: Bob Grimm

reviews.text: The cast is fantastic.
reviews.author: May Leitz

reviews.text: fascinating and perverse and never boring, but it's not really compelling either because it remains abstract and theoretical and too obviously staged.
reviews.author: James Kendrick

reviews.text: 'The Lighthouse' will challenge, delight art-house fans.
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: The story gets downright insane. To call The Lighthouse bonkers would be an understatement, and Eggers thrives on the disorientation.
reviews.author: Alan French

reviews.text: Like many others, I am fascinated by lighthouses and their construction, especially those equipped with large Fresnel lenses which are things of beauty. This movie kind of spoiled all that for me. It is a boring and unpleasant movie to sit through.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: By the time we come to the end of this 110-minute journey, like the film's protagonists, the audience feels like it has ascended from some sort of cinema hell.
reviews.author: Joe Friar

reviews.text: One of the year's best films. Surreal, powerfully acted, and proves that Robert Eggers is one of the premiere arthouse horror directors working today.
reviews.author: Drew Dietsch

reviews.text: The Lighthouse is a fascinating work... a risky and unconventional project. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Iván Belmont

reviews.text: Eggers assembles a legitimate, weirdly fascinating pitch-dark horror picture that spirals beyond human comprehension.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: As much as "The Lighthouse" gets cinematically right, there's at least one thing that it gets wrong: it certainly isn't accessible.
reviews.author: Richard Bonaduce

reviews.text: A black-and-white mood piece in which two men frequently talk while sitting at the dinner table. That might make this sound like My Dinner with Andre, except that art-house hit inexplicably didn't make room for a mermaid in its tale.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: A total exercise in style, brought to glorious excess by showy performances and visual gimmicks right out of an ambitious nightmare.
reviews.author: David Keyes

reviews.text: The Lighthouse is a movie you can either dissect to find meaning or bathe in the atmosphere. I can't say you'll enjoy it, but you should appreciate it.
reviews.author: Jeff Owens

reviews.text: You go into "The Lighthouse" not knowing what to expect, with (director Robert) Eggers heightening that feeling by playing off your anticipation of what you think lies ahead.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: Like The Witch, it is bleakly realistic with mythical or supernatural overtones, but both aspects are heightened, the real elements darker, and the mystical or imaginary aspects expanded and laid out in shocking and unexpected ways.
reviews.author: Monica Reid

reviews.text: As the story unfolds, Eggers almost effortlessly conveys viewer curiosities about the veil separating the corporeal and the ethereal.
reviews.author: Greg Carlson

reviews.text: The Lighthouse isn't a film you can digest right away; it's a movie to talk about later, and enjoy, or shrink from, at your leisure.
reviews.author: Jay Stone

reviews.text: With Willem Dafoe and Robert Pattinson, Eggers' intransigent vision is backed by two fabulous actors whose interaction adds to the threatening and desperate atmosphere of the film. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: The Lighthouse doesn't have much of a plot beyond "Things are bad and getting worse." But the conflict between the principals keeps us engaged, aided by their florid dialogue.
reviews.author: Margot Harrison

reviews.text: A bold, risk-taking work from a true cinematic visionary.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: The unrelenting soundscape does terrific work in creating space for the rest of the film to work its hallucinatory magic.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: A turgid, miserable, homoerotic dirge...
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: Like Pattinson's Ephraim, The Lighthouse is weird, complex, testing... and soulless.
reviews.author: Adam Kempenaar

reviews.text: True folklore.
reviews.author: Evan Dossey

reviews.text: It doesn't have the succinct terrors of his first film but it offers much of the same kind of unsettling tropes, set against an even more pitiless locale.
reviews.author: Piers Marchant

reviews.text: An artful fever dream of drunken confessions, delirious hallucinations, mermaid sex and farts.
reviews.author: Annlee Ellingson

reviews.text: [A] startling, darkly funny maritime nightmare.
reviews.author: Teresa Nieman

reviews.text: I can see the film driving many audience members as batty as its characters, but just as many will undoubtedly fall under its hypnotic spell.
reviews.author: Adam Lubitow

reviews.text: I'm certainly not going to give anything away-I do not need a curse from Triton right now-but I think that if you like your horror weird and knotty and kinda psychological, this is going to be your favorite movie of the year.
reviews.author: Leah Schnelbach

reviews.text: It is a relentless, intoxicating fight of two men fumbling after the light and receding deeper into darkness.
reviews.author: Leonardo Goi

reviews.text: The Lighthouse is as downright unsettling, as totally disturbing, as any black-and-white nightmare since David Lynch's Eraserhead.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: Let there be light.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: You'll not soon see another film so rich in cultural references. Visually, The Lighthouse is a knockout.
reviews.author: Erica Abeel

reviews.text: Things get weird, and sad, and unexpectedly touching; Dafoe and Pattinson are both great, and if you're going to descend into Eggers's particular brand of fraught, bleak madness, one could hardly ask for better company.
reviews.author: Erik Henriksen

reviews.text: One of the year's best. An example of the kind of intelligent, innovative filmmaking that should be cherished and championed.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: The Lighthouse is one of the boldest genre films of 2019.
reviews.author: Heather Wixson

reviews.text: Lands squarely on the ideal side of weird and, although often maddening to watch, it happily never sinks to the most irritating levels of cinematic pretension that often suffocates most art house fare.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: ...a cinematic sailor's yarn you won't soon forget.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: It is a dark, brooding, disgusting, masterpiece of a film.
reviews.author: Brittany Knupper

reviews.text: What becomes clear early on is that rather than searching for stable truth or rational explanation, The Lighthouse is a film in which the only option is to give oneself over fully to its haunting, mesmeric dream-logic.
reviews.author: Dave Platt

reviews.text: To say that The Lighthouse leaves you wondering what the hell did you just witness is an understatement.
reviews.author: Marianna Neal

reviews.text: Pattinson and Dafoe give two of the best performances of their careers, putting seemingly every emotion on display throughout the film.
reviews.author: Ian Thomas Malone

reviews.text: With a solid story, excellent performances, and a truly masterful approach to claustrophobic filmmaking, The Lighthouse is a strong effort for everyone involved.
reviews.author: Gabriel Ricard

reviews.text: It's very clear that both men are lonely. A sense of eroticism pervades what becomes maniacal behavior. The necessary closeness of their living conditions provokes anger. Is Thomas jealous of Ephraim's youth and beauty?
reviews.author: Michael Calleri

reviews.text: Shocking and a lot of fun.
reviews.author: Diane Carson

reviews.text: "The Lighthouse" is a work of atmosphere, using stark visuals - in this case, black and white imagery shot at an unusual square aspect ratio - and a scant soundtrack to build an unsettling atmosphere of dread.
reviews.author: Josh Terry

reviews.text: How much The Lighthouse works or doesn't depends entirely on your perspective; there's perhaps no film currently in theaters that so catalyzes the subjectivity of art.
reviews.author: Lauren Humphries-Brooks

reviews.text: Wild and unhinged, The Lighthouse may not be entirely comprehensible, but it sends you out of the theater in a way that colors perception, making your surroundings look more alien, more forbidding.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: From the opening frames of The Lighthouse, it sits with you. It is haunting. Eerie. As the two men wander through their daily duties on the island, Eggers manages to find the horror in the mundane.
reviews.author: Kimberly Pierce

reviews.text: It's a good thing Willem Dafoe and Robert Pattinson deliver indelible performances in this aggressively foreboding chiller, because "The Witch" director Robert Eggers tries so hard to channel Melville and Lovecraft that he loses his grip on the material.
reviews.author: Rubén Rosario

reviews.text: Eggers balances the film's darkly religious and malevolently Freudian themes by portraying the visceral realities of two men scrunched together in ramshackle surroundings on an island of rain and rock.
reviews.author: Rick Levin

reviews.text: The ambiguity of this movie is what makes it feel special.
reviews.author: Chris Stuckmann

reviews.text: Willem Dafoe and Robert Pattinson are brutally antagonistic toward each other in riveting performances as lighthouse keepers in this disturbing but enthralling film enhanced by the austere setting shot in black and white.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: Robert Eggers' "The Lighthouse" won't be for the faint of heart - or those who crave a tidy narrative - but his hallucinatory fever-dream is indeed an experience at the movies.
reviews.author: Matthew Passantino

reviews.text: The Lighthouse is a triumph of filmmaking, though it's a very, very strange triumph.
reviews.author: Tim Brennan

reviews.text: Two oddballs sittin' 'round talkin' and some other things is more creepy-crawly than scary in the hands of artsy director Eggars and his two fine actors.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: A dark and twisted fever dream of a film that confronts the anguish of the human condition with suitable horror and an equally suitable dash of absurdity
reviews.author: Andrea Chase

reviews.text: Those who are looking for some cinematic craziness and ambitiousness will most likely love The Lighthouse.
reviews.author: Michelle Kisner

reviews.text: The actors play it big and bold in a visually striking, black and white horror show.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: The visceral, disgusting, and irrefutably maddening theatrics of The Lighthouse are entrancing enough to have viewers happily giving themselves over to a beckoning siren by film's end.
reviews.author: Cody Corrall

reviews.text: Harrowing, haunting and suspenseful.
reviews.author: Michael Smith

reviews.text: Like "The Witch," not all audiences are going to be buying what Eggers is selling, but "The Lighthouse" isn't lacking in audacity or originality. And I, for one, can't wait to see what the director will do for his next trick.
reviews.author: Brad Keefe

reviews.text: A mesmerizing film that's also pleasurably mystifying.... It might baffle you, but its visceral impact is undeniable.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: The Lighthouse works because of the strength of the actors' performances, the power of their interaction, and the aura of incipient dread that saturates everything.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: Eggers is having such a blast employing old silent film techniques and finding new textures in old settings that one hopes he stays in this new lane he's carved for himself, telling tales set as far away from modernity as possible.
reviews.author: Dominic Griffin

reviews.text: You willl feel like you are living with two men in a giant phallus in a solitary spot in the middle of the sea. Who's Afraid of Spongebob Squarepants?
reviews.author: David Poland

reviews.text: It's rough going, but it's beautifully filmed and framed in black and white, and Dafoe is wild and wildly entertaining in a role that feels written to match his every aspect.
reviews.author: Matthew Lickona

reviews.text: Filmed on location in Nova Scotia, the images are the most gorgeously bleak this side of early Ingmar Bergman. Pattinson, it turns out, was meant to be photographed in diffused black-and-white.
reviews.author: Randall King

reviews.text: A mesmerizing visual feast...and a rudderless waste of time.
reviews.author: Jeff Mitchell

reviews.text: This film features the darkest tendencies of masculine impulses arising to redefine the world as we know it, consuming everything in a reaction of blunt-force violence.
reviews.author: Jason Shawhan

reviews.text: A descent into madness worth taking.
reviews.author: Kyle Pinion

reviews.text: The Lighthouse is an incredibly unique, utterly bizarre film, an almost mythic tale that could inspire a sea shanty or five.
reviews.author: Lee Jutton

reviews.text: The Lighthouse is a trip, a harrowing journey into the minds of two men who drive each other insane while locked up together with the weather raging outside.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: Director-writer Robert Eggers loves playing mind games in "The Lighthouse," a psychological thriller that could very well be a tantalizing, creepy alternative to a lot of Halloween movie fare.
reviews.author: George M. Thomas

reviews.text: The Lighthouse is a riveting, well-acted, and impressively made movie, and I never want to see it again.
reviews.author: Hannah Lynn

reviews.text: The look is always striking, it is certainly a lot funnier than one might expect (albeit in the most mordant manner possible) and the two leads play very well off of each other.
reviews.author: Peter Sobczynski

reviews.text: Maybe too knowing. It tired me out at times. But it has a strong afterlife in the mind, like a briny shanty recalled at night.
reviews.author: Robert Horton

reviews.text: Dafoe not only chews up the scenery around him, he bites down hard on it, chips a tooth, swallows it whole and lets out a massive belch.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: Their fights are amazingly physical and psychological in a horror picture that ends more or less like Kubrick's "2001."
reviews.author: Barry Paris

reviews.text: Pattinson is superb but it's Dafoe who emerges as a giant with a towering, unforgettable performance.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: The director of 'The Witch' returns, bringing us deep into the heart of pretentious art house cinema.
reviews.author: Christian Toto

reviews.text: "The Lighthouse" is a punishing film with a miserable conclusion; it's only recommended to those willing to wallow in its sad view of men running from guilt and finding no quarter.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: The Lighthouse is a marvel of filmmaking and outstanding acting.
reviews.author: Nicolás Delgadillo

reviews.text: The Lighthouse is, for better and for worse, a maddening experience, indeed.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Even with a finale as rocky as the shoreline on which Thomas and Ephraim are stranded, the film is an absolute must-see, a brilliant shining beacon in a sea of stagnant cinema, guiding viewers through the storm toward salvation.
reviews.author: Brent Hankins

reviews.text: It is scary, sure, but not in any of the ways you think of as enjoyable; it's troubling, dark and unsettling. In other words, it's very good.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: What is the opposite of a crowd-pleaser? A crowd-splitter, maybe? Whatever you call it, "The Lighthouse" is one.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: "The Lighthouse" feels terrifying due to its remoteness and distance from the present.
reviews.author: Garrett Mitchell

reviews.text: The Lighthouse an interesting movie; it's the performances that make it a good one.
reviews.author: Matthew Monagle

reviews.text: 'The Lighthouse' is a challenging experience that will make your mind run amok, to the point where you begin to feel it slipping away like its characters.
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: Is this about madness? Nature unleashed? A fever dream? Are we in hell? You can make a case for any or all of these and more. It's bonkers and a hell of a film.
reviews.author: Karen Gordon

reviews.text: Eggers goes further, with cinematographer Jarin Blaschke shooting in black-and-white 35 millimeter film, in an almost square frame, to add to the claustrophobic atmosphere that seems to be driving both men insane.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: Adrift on a cinematic sea? I pray Robert Eggers' Lighthouse doesn't become your beacon. You'll be dashed to death on the rocks of pretension.
reviews.author: Cameron Meier

reviews.text: ...there is nothing else like The Lighthouse this year.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: Like the worst nightmares, it's an experience you might come away from hoping never to revisit, and it'll haunt you long after it's over.
reviews.author: Matthew Singer

reviews.text: It is a cult classic in the making, with the potential to be our generation's version of the The Rocky Horror Picture Show.
reviews.author: Anne Cohen

reviews.text: People who signed up for a grim historical drama may be shocked. But for many, it will hopefully be a welcome surprise.
reviews.author: Gavia Baker-Whitelaw

reviews.text: Those Eggers boys really have a way with words.
reviews.author: Danielle Del Plato

reviews.text: Powerful images and even more potent acting are the hallmarks of The Lighthouse.
reviews.author: Ken Eisner

reviews.text: Pattison and Dafoe provide moments of unhinged chemistry... Yet, it's Eggers' film that feels self-satisfying to a fault.
reviews.author: Glenn Heath Jr.

reviews.text: All the rib-nudging phallic imagery makes 'The Lighthouse' feel like the world's most elaborate penis joke, cackling at the erect, elongated title structure and the seamen stuck inside, ready to blow.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: It's a cinematic sea shanty, made of equal parts joviality and menace, slurring every word.
reviews.author: Hunter Lanier

reviews.text: "The Lighthouse" may be a little too in love with its own virtuosity, but who can blame it? At a time when American movies are overrun with shopworn visions, its madness is a balm and a beacon.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: Depending on the scene, Eggers' wild, nervy film might convey its ideas with dense existential dread, repulsive fantasy visuals, or utterly deranged slapstick.
reviews.author: Andrew Wyatt

reviews.text: Picturesque but tiresome.
reviews.author: Kelly Vance

reviews.text: The Lighthouse may not register with those turned off by the bizarre or in need of a more conventional storyline, but [writer-director Robert] Eggers ... continues to redefine the horror genre and inject it with an arthouse flair.
reviews.author: Kiko Martinez

reviews.text: Driven by its stars' maniacal performances, The Lighthouse makes for an impeccably crafted, though thematically uneven, blend of horror and humor.
reviews.author: Sandy Schaefer

reviews.text: The Lighthouse immerses you in its disturbing environment and enthralling performances of its two-man cast. Robert Pattinson and Willem Dafoe push the acting craft to the brink.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: A Bergmanesque trip down the rabbit hole of psychological horror with mesmerizing cinematography. It's bold, bizarre and brilliant.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: I admire it, but I don't particularly love it... Technically, it is an extraordinary achievement, but it's still kind of a mini-Twilight Zone experiment.
reviews.author: Wade Major

reviews.text: These are actors who take chances. They are taking chances together [in The Lighthouse], and it is thrilling to watch.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: Striking as Ephraim's epic battle with a seagull and his various hallucinatory visions may be, a handful of haunting sights aren't enough to make a successful film.
reviews.author: Edwin Arnaudin

reviews.text: We leave the theatre feeling like we've been through something, even if we may not be able to articulate exactly what the hell it was.
reviews.author: Abbie Bernstein

reviews.text: "The Lighthouse" is challenging but not dense, visually immersive in a tricky way we welcome because few movies these days are so creative.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: Once again, [Robert] Eggers proves at expert at bringing elemental cultural touchstones to vivid life on-screen.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: ...a brutal but lyrical 19th century horror show
reviews.author: Chris Barsanti

reviews.text: An engrossing and bizarre experience from Robert Eggers, The Lighthouse is one of the best films in the last decade. This must be seen to be believed.
reviews.author: EJ Moreno

reviews.text: Robert Eggers delivers a hypnotic, horror-thriller with masterful performances from Robert Pattinson and Willem Dafoe as lighthouse attendance descending into madness. Eggers uses Gorgeous cinematography of surrounding sea as third silent character.
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: Willem Dafoe and Robert Pattinson act up a storm in a wild descent into madness. Thank god for Black and White movies.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: Eggers's madness has too little method behind it; it might captivate some purely for its weirdness, but it stands little chance of standing the test of time.
reviews.author: Nathanael Hood

reviews.text: ..."The Lighthouse" is a film that shows Eggers' technical strength perfectly, even if it loses its characters in it.
reviews.author: Kate Sánchez

reviews.text: Mesmerizing, intense and disturbing arthouse psychological black and white horror pic.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: Eggers' moody, esoteric descent into madness is a showcase for two gifted actors at the height of their powers.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: The Lighthouse﻿ is such an effective exercise in projecting claustrophobia, in both a physical and psychological sense, that it'd be unbearable to watch if it weren't so funny.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: An immaculately curated film, but that's not quite the same thing as the inexact science of direction, and the result is a movie too overwrought and worried-over to convey the sense of either loneliness or claustrophobia that it strains toward.
reviews.author: Nick Pinkerton

reviews.text: As striking as the performances within The Lighthouse are, Egger's technique is even more astounding as he musters an atmosphere that sucks audiences into the muck and madness of his movie.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: A movie designed to shiver your timbers and fog your mind.
reviews.author: Kurt Loder

reviews.text: A delirious, enigmatic and deranged gem about isolation and guilt. Pattinson and Dafoe's stunning face-off is one for the ages. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: The Lighthouse is persistently intense, emotionally nerve-wracking, unnervingly horny, and surprisingly funny at times.
reviews.author: Leigh Monson

reviews.text: A fabulous, unnerving sea chantey meant to rattle us with slow-burning madness.
reviews.author: Eric D. Snider

reviews.text: It's funny, high-spirited, and giddily loopy, a descent into madness told with the energy of a sea shanty.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: It sees its creator ably beating the sophomore jinx, sustaining a mood that's every bit as entrancingly eerie as The Witch's.
reviews.author: Michael Gingold

reviews.text: The Lighthouse is guaranteed to be unlike anything you've seen before.
reviews.author: Laura Potier

reviews.text: A more perfect role for Willem Dafoe does not and may never exist, but it's hard not to wish that there was a little more story to go with the admittedly incredible scene setting.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: A haunting tale that chilled me to me bones!
reviews.author: Rosalie Kicks

reviews.text: It is a rare treat to watch great actors abandon the pretense of safety and good taste.
reviews.author: Alan Zilberman

reviews.text: The Lighthouse Shines Brightly into a Narrative Void.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: Dafoe and Pattinson have the stage pretty much to themselves, and the result is a beguiling crunch of styles.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: It's an intense, strange movie that got me thinking
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: It doesn't illuminate new or fascinating corners of the horror genre, but the actors blind you with their incandescent talent. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Nestor Bentancor

reviews.text: The Lighthouse is, among many other things, very funny in its pitch-dark fashion, and atmospheric in a way that's rarely seen, or felt, on the screen.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: Director Robert Eggers has crafted a psychological thriller practically spat up by hell itself, and it is supremely unpleasant in the best way possible.
reviews.author: Matthew Dougherty

reviews.text: Pattinson and Dafoe dig into their roles... [and] Together with Eggers they deliver a masterful study of souls trapped on a rock alone, but also trapped together, with all the twisty complexities involved.
reviews.author: Tom Russo

reviews.text: Director Robert Eggers' emotional powerhouse, The Lighthouse, is a profound allegorical reminder that no man is an island.
reviews.author: J.R. Kinnard

reviews.text: Has abject misery ever been such fun to watch? Has soul-sick dread ever looked so gorgeous?
reviews.author: Glen Weldon

reviews.text: ...mood and brood and it is not enough to prevent The Lighthouse from disappearing in the fog.
reviews.author: Dana Barbuto

reviews.text: Both the tension and the maniacal comedy build steadily over the entire running time, like a Fawlty Towers episode written by H.P. Lovecraft.
reviews.author: Oscar Goff

reviews.text: "The Lighthouse" is a senses-riveting immersion, aurally awash in the sonorous sounds of the sea, the pelt of torrential rain and the soul-shaking roar of the title structure's bullhorn.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: A black-and-white fever dream of a film that keels between sea shanty and psychodrama, with heavy doses of the absurd.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: At its finest, and creepiest, "The Lighthouse" courts comparison (at least in ambition) to F.W. Murnau's fantasies of temptation, desire and striking imagery.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: There is not enough compelling story, mystery, or perversion to fill or overwhelm this eerie environment.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: Eggers meticulously sets the scene, adds texture and builds tension and mystery from men locked in battle and sometimes in embrace.
reviews.author: Manohla Dargis

reviews.text: The Lighthouse is a grandiose work of art that is as haunting as it is funny.
reviews.author: Shannon McGrew

reviews.text: "The Lighthouse" is a triumph of mood and vision, like the love child of Andrei Tarkovsky and David Lynch that knows that its actors are just a small piece of the overall composition.
reviews.author: Lindsey Bahr

reviews.text: Two primal performances from Willem Dafoe and Robert Pattinson carry Robert Eggers' second film to glory. Stunningly shot in black and white in the boxy format common in the silent era, The Lighthouse seeps into your bones with a power that won't let go.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: You won't be able to describe this movie to your friends. But you may love it.
reviews.author: Dana Kennedy

reviews.text: This at first fascinating and never less than bonkers movie is eventually sunk by its own theological overreach.
reviews.author: Dana Stevens

reviews.text: Leave two men on an island together, and things will likely become fraught very quickly - and this film takes that to a whole new level.
reviews.author: Jenny Desborough

reviews.text: In a cinematic age defined by the sequel, remake and reboot, this filmmaker's idiosyncratic vision represents a beacon of light shining through the mist.
reviews.author: Thomas Floyd

reviews.text: Once again, Eggers and his crew have gone far lengths to develop a film unlike a lot of what is seen in the sphere of genre features today.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: "The Lighthouse" has only enough story to fill a 25-minute "Zone" episode, and that's including next week's coming attractions and two obligatory and very-welcome monologues by Rod Serling.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: The Lighthouse feels like an old sea captain's folk tale, passed down through generations to scare the landlubbers away.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: The kind of bold, bleak, dizzying experimentation only a filmmaker with Eggers' cultural capital could attempt.
reviews.author: Clint Worthington

reviews.text: Eggers mixes a sense of grim fatality with an odd bit of humor here and there, especially when flatulence comes into play. "The Lighthouse" is miles away from "The Witch."
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: In "The Lighthouse," Eggers stages a battle of wills between two men in isolation and leaves it up to us whether the outcome is determined by mythology or madness...a quirky piece of work with one hell of an undertow.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: Has the bearing an old silent film based on a sea shanty told by sailors to pass the time on a cold, dreary night.
reviews.author: Matt Singer

reviews.text: You can almost smell the salt and grime. This is sensory, claustrophobic filmmaking.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: The Lighthouse defies rational description. Shot in black and white in Academy ratio, on screen it's dark, grimy and claustrophobic.
reviews.author: Alexa Dalby

reviews.text: This might sound crass, but there's a true metaphor here: The Lighthouse loves the smell of its own farts (not necessarily a negative, either).
reviews.author: Matt Donato

reviews.text: Eggers again proves masterful at bringing the impossibilities of antiquity to life. Like the infertile New England woods before it, the ocean is this film's untamable frontier, where men stand at the mercy of nature and dream of salvation.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: If you're looking for a wild ride, here it be.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: A first-rate film experience. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alberto Sáez Villarino

reviews.text: The Lighthouse is utterly unlike anything else you could see this year, a resounding crash of myth and grime that absolutely has to be seen to be believed.
reviews.author: Jack Blackwell

reviews.text: As richly absorbing as it is visionary, The Lighthouse is an unforgettable mood piece and astonishing showcase for its two stars.
reviews.author: Shaun Munro

reviews.text: The Lighthouse is Robert Egger's masterpiece of mythic quality. It is one of the greatest achievements in cinema this year and is an unstoppable force of dark and maddening confinement.
reviews.author: Ben Rolph

reviews.text: Eggers balances its nightmarish grimness with humour in the bleak tradition of a British kitchen-sink sitcom, a Beckett play, and the aforementioned Withnail and I.
reviews.author: Nicholas Barber

reviews.text: Thankfully, Dafoe and Pattinson were practically made for this film, and chew up every square inch of the screen for all 110 minutes.
reviews.author: Justin Jones

reviews.text: With elements of the gothic, dark fairy-tale, and incomprehensible handling of time, The Lighthouse remains incredibly elusive throughout, which only serves to make it more hypnotic as it weaves its dark web before it reaches its chilling climax.
reviews.author: Lewis Knight

reviews.text: The beans are spilled; The Lighthouse is no sophomore slump for The Witch director Robert Eggers, here going full-blown insane with a treasure trove of unsettling imagery and a pair of outstanding boisterous performances
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: THE LIGHTHOUSE may get lost in its own myths, but it still underscores Robert Eggers as a phenomenal talent who will continue to surprise and grow with each work he creates.
reviews.author: Rob Dean

reviews.text: "The Lighthouse" is not easy viewing in any capacity, but it is one of the most wild, distinctive movie-going experiences I've had all year.
reviews.author: Matt Shiverdecker

reviews.text: With endlessly engaging imagery and two remarkable lead performances, The Lighthouse all but assures the legacy of Eggers in the arthouse horror genre.
reviews.author: Audrey Fox

reviews.text: ...the film follows a nightmarish logic all its own, enveloping you in noise and shadow until you can practically feel the salt spray and smell the chamberpots.
reviews.author: Angie Han

reviews.text: ...what that creature and her sexual allure do in the context of this story is to highlight the ways the beautiful and grotesque all too often intersect. It's the theme at the heart of The Lighthouse and one executed with such potency.
reviews.author: Kayleigh Donaldson

reviews.text: A spiritual and visual delirium not suitable for all stomachs. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: While THE LIGHTHOUSE is full of atmosphere, Robert Eggers fails to fill that atmosphere with a compelling story.
reviews.author: Alan Cerny

reviews.text: The purest joy it provides is watching two stellar actors engaging in psychological warfare for the duration of the film.
reviews.author: Germain Lussier

reviews.text: A visceral ride, The Lighthouse explores man's relationship to the sea, specifically through the lens of backbreaking labor.
reviews.author: Joelle Monique

reviews.text: A dark fable full of creative freedom and wrapped up by two great actors. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jonay Armas

reviews.text: An exceptional film. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Álex Manzano

reviews.text: [A] duet of delicious artifice and audacity...
reviews.author: Chris Feil

reviews.text: For better or for worse, The Lighthouse features two gifted actors going off the rails.
reviews.author: Victor Stiff

reviews.text: The Lighthouse slowly snakes its way through your mind, gripping tighter until you relinquish all expectations and succumb to the strange, haunting glory of this wild ride.
reviews.author: Oliver Whitney

reviews.text: You'll never really figure out just what the hell is going on in The Lighthouse, but it's one of the few cases where a lot of confusion isn't too much of a bad thing.
reviews.author: Andrea Thompson

reviews.text: If THE LIGHTHOUSE works it's because Dafoe and Pattinson perform beyond all expectation, as there's nothing else to do with the material but go overboard with it.
reviews.author: Rubin Safaya

reviews.text: Stunning, upsetting, funny, and weird, The Lighthouse is a masterpiece of both minimalism and grandiose vision.
reviews.author: Kyle Anderson

reviews.text: As a rumination on loneliness, desolation, and madness, The Lighthouse is filled to the brim with disturbing dialogue and haunting images that will burrow into your brain.
reviews.author: Chris Tilly

reviews.text: The two stormy performances by Willem Dafoe and Robert Pattinson that are so touched by madness that the cracks in their unblinking stares, and crusty whiskers, cast an unreality all their own.
reviews.author: David Crow

reviews.text: You don't watch The Lighthouse. You absorb it. Pattinson and Dafoe are like caged animals slinking around the perimeter, testing each other's resolve before pouncing.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: There is something of Mikhail Bakhtin's carnivalesque in the way things transpire: a free revelry in what is base, taboo and profane, right down to the coded foreplay within Pattinson and Dafoe's later interactions.
reviews.author: Tomas Trussow

reviews.text: By turns funny, sinister, haunting, historically fascinating and mythical, "The Lighthouse" is one of the best films of the year.
reviews.author: Sara Stewart

reviews.text: How effective would a descent into madness be if it made sense?
reviews.author: David Bax

reviews.text: It is buckwild and vivid, funny and freaky.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: ...this phantasmagoria plays the audience like a fiddle, weaving a deeply unsettling sea shanty.
reviews.author: Jonathan Barkan

reviews.text: While there are suggestive images and funny moments of macabre hallucination, the subject becomes tiresome. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Leonardo Garcia Tsao

reviews.text: The Lighthouse is a stunning sophomore effort for Eggers, featuring two exceptional performances by Dafoe and Pattinson and a stunning visual and aural aesthetic. It's an awards season shoe-in and deservedly so.
reviews.author: Joe Lipsett

reviews.text: The Lighthouse  pales in comparison to Eggers previous film The Witch, keeping his audience anticipating some climax than never arrives.
reviews.author: Dustin Chase

reviews.text: "The Lighthouse" will give certain audience members the intoxicating aftertaste of a gothic sensation, while others could walk away in frustration. That's exactly how Robert Eggers wants it.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: The Lighthouse features two very strong performances from both Willem Dafoe and Robert Pattinson in this beautifully shot movie.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: You will be dreaming of beards, corncob pipes, blinding light, and tentacles for days. Consider that a warning, or an enticement.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: Robert Eggers' film The Lighthouse is one of those projects that leaves you pondering if you're sick for liking it, but at the same time, you might feel bad if you don't.
reviews.author: Adriana Gomez-Weston

reviews.text: Something wild, horrific and drop-dead gorgeous that will send cinephiles everywhere into orgasmic fits.
reviews.author: Zhuo-Ning Su

reviews.text: Is it horror? Comedy? Is it a meditation on the madness of driven men, shot through with lashings of Lovecraftian dread? It's all of those, and something else besides.
reviews.author: Norman Wilner

reviews.text: While Eggers' distinct vision is astonishing, the film thrives thanks to the fearless work by Dafoe and Pattinson.
reviews.author: Courtney Small

reviews.text: Beautifully shot and acted. An athmospheric horror movie that bring to mind Val Lewton.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: An intriguing premise and stellar performances by the two actors are the shining lights of the film, but it tends to deviate too much to pay off in the end.
reviews.author: Ashley Menzel

reviews.text: It's very impressive that Robert Pattinson has the acting chops to keep up with Willem Dafoe in the crazy department.
reviews.author: Jason Guerrasio

reviews.text: While it's ultimately a bit too self-conscious to provoke the existential dread and true terror of the best films like it, it's still an impressive accomplishment thanks to Eggers' fearlessness and a pair of completely committed performances.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: Many audiences are going to be utterly shocked at the lengths the two leading actors, Pattinson, Dafoe, are pushed. They have a loathsome dynamic. However, those who can get on Eggers' level will be hypnotized by this eccentric experiment.
reviews.author: James Clay

reviews.text: The Lighthouse boasts and thrives off of a maritime rap battle between Willem Dafoe and Robert Pattison, whose claustrophobic journey together towards madness is among the sickest and most memorable collaborations in recent memory.
reviews.author: Luke Parker

reviews.text: The nutty, get under your skin quasi-horror bromance The Lighthouse starring Robert Pattinson and Willem Dafoe is a trip.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: If it's possible for a movie made with impeccable craft to be boring and even enervating, here's a candidate.
reviews.author: Adam Nayman

reviews.text: Too weird for words but highly entertaining for anyone willing to get on side with its nasty, misanthropic wavelength.
reviews.author: Andrew Parker

reviews.text: It's Dafoe who steals the show. His Efraim is damn-near horrific to behold, a behemoth of a presence with his unkempt beard, ridiculous pirate accent and toxic machoism.
reviews.author: Jordan Ruimy

reviews.text: There are moments where Pattinson is so transformative it's jarring. You simply never thought he had it in him.
reviews.author: Gregory Ellwood

reviews.text: 'The Lighthouse' leaves in the spectator a genuine deposit of admiration, especially towards the actors committed to a gale of dialogues and physical prowess. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Manu Yáñez

reviews.text: If not for Pattinson and Dafoe being two of the world's most recognizable working actors, I would believe this could be some recently unearthed treasure from an earlier era of filmmaking.
reviews.author: Emma Stefansky

reviews.text: The interplay between the two men plays out teasingly, with an Oedipal tension between tyro and patriarch that plays out at times like a maritime, rum-soaked version of Steptoe and Son.
reviews.author: Jonathan Romney

reviews.text: The triumph of The Lighthouse lies not only in its darkness, but in how it illuminates the fragility and terror of its characters in front of our eyes.
reviews.author: Manuela Lazic

reviews.text: It is a truly unbelievable film, achieving depths of cerebral insanity horror has rarely breached and impregnating it with a dark sense of comedic absurdity to allow viewers some semblance of stability as the plot derails into nautical oblivion.
reviews.author: Luke Hicks

reviews.text: The Lighthouse is a dizzying, joyous celebration, a riot of smell and clanging noise dressed up in formally austere arthouse clothing, whose unsettling crescendo of derangement pushes the spectator into a state of semi-rapture.
reviews.author: Caspar Salmon

reviews.text: Peerless filmmaking from a director who's emerging as one of contemporary horror's true greats.
reviews.author: Jordan Farley

reviews.text: A psychological nightmare that gnaws at the brain long after the disturbing final image assaults the retina.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: A high-level aesthetic bet. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Daniel de Partearroyo

reviews.text: With The Lighthouse [Robert] Eggers delivers another formally exciting and evocative feature, it's an immersive cinematic experience that luxuriates in filthy masculinity as tyrannical power struggle.
reviews.author: Katherine McLaughlin

reviews.text: A rapturously-bleak horror/fantasy...
reviews.author: Stephen Garrett

reviews.text: The end result leaves more doubts than truth. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge (JJ) Negrete

reviews.text: An oppressive, richly textured slow-burn of a psychological thriller, pitched somewhere between a silent cinema chiller and a Roman Polanski classic.
reviews.author: Allan Hunter

reviews.text: It leaves you dazed, terrified and elated, and it signals Eggers as one of the most exciting directors working today.
reviews.author: Joseph Walsh

reviews.text: A radical and fascinating film. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: The picture ploughs through centuries of lore for briny manifestations of madness. All are cleverly imagined. Many are properly unsettling.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: A relentless piece of maritime madness, with transcendent performances from Robert Pattinson and Willem Dafoe.
reviews.author: Iana Murray

reviews.text: Eggers has created a film of disturbing horror, absurdist comedy and probing psychodrama which defies the generic boundaries as it breaks through them. The Lighthouse is a saltwater gothic masterpiece.
reviews.author: John Bleasdale

reviews.text: An inevitable acting tour de force by Robert Pattinson and Willem Dafoe. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juanma Ruiz

reviews.text: Dialogues... respond both to a deeply literary character and to an old English whose purpose is not so much the dramatic development as the brilliance of its actors [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jaime Pena

reviews.text: Shot in a jagged, expressionist black and white, this is chiaroscuro with the emphasis on scuro, and confirms writer-director Robert Eggers as a major talent.
reviews.author: Raphael Abraham

reviews.text: Robert Eggers loosens the noose of veracity that choked his meticulously researched but painfully self-serious debut just enough to allow for so much absurdism to peek through.
reviews.author: Sam C. Mac

reviews.text: The Lighthouse douses us with its sickly brine, with cruelty and comeuppance the catch of the day.
reviews.author: Jason Gorber

reviews.text: The failures in the film's narrative don't make it a true misstep. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alonso Díaz de la Vega

reviews.text: The Lighthouse takes on masculinity, madness and merfolk, and it's marvelous.
reviews.author: Gus Edgar

reviews.text: Not since the Overlook hotel appeared on screen has any piece of remote real estate been so ominous and obviously dangerous as the simple, weather-beaten lighthouse on the coast of Maine that sits atop a cragged landscape in Robert Eggers' new film.
reviews.author: Luiz Oliveira

reviews.text: Probably the most delightful thing about The Lighthouse is that it gives Willem Dafoe the role of a lifetime.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: Dafoe, especially, digs his maw deep into Eggers' stylishly, flavorfully archaic dialogue, in a performance that suggests a live-action version of the sea captain from The Simpsons.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: A stunning piece of work, with two exceptional performances at its heart. The Lighthouse is a superlative piece of filmmaking on every level
reviews.author: Jo-Ann Titmarsh

reviews.text: Eggers leans hard into the Kubrick vibe, but unlike his many peers attempting the same, he has the narrative originality and technical expertise to see it through.
reviews.author: Charles Bramesco

reviews.text: Pattinson and Dafoe pull off the dynamic, managing the remarkable feat of making a two-hour movie feel no sparser for having only two people in it.
reviews.author: Karen Han

reviews.text: At least Pattinson and Dafoe's admirably invested work will linger, two actors losing themselves just a little bit as their characters lose it all.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: Channeling elements of German Expressionism, Franz Kafka, Herman Melville and a wild dollop of Greek mythology, this tale of isolation and insanity, is an ambitious and unheralded cinematic joy to behold.
reviews.author: Nicholas Bell

reviews.text: It's as if this footage has just been unearthed after a century mouldering in a Scandinavian documentary film archive.
reviews.author: Michael Leader

reviews.text: It has the feel of a newly discovered artefact from FW Murnau (Nosferatu).
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: Eggers' vision here transcends conventional categorization-it is a historico-psychological-existential thriller; a bewildering, boozy bloody bromance; a sea-soaked single-location supernatural suspense story. It is, in short, A Lot To Take In.
reviews.author: Joel Mayward

reviews.text: A film that feels less made than hoisted up like treasure from the belly of some rust-bitten shipwreck.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: Claustrophobic cacophony reigns supreme - the rest of this year's titles will have to furiously paddle to try and compete.
reviews.author: Ella Kemp

reviews.text: Its reimagining of the hysterical psychodrama as the province not of women, in whose febrile brains such tales have traditionally been located, but of men, it's shimmeringly contemporary, and has real long-game sustain.
reviews.author: Jessica Kiang

reviews.text: There is nothing as unnerving as the most striking sequences in The Witch - in fact, for the more adventurous genre audiences out there, this unpredictable ride could constitute the year's most unlikely crowd pleaser.
reviews.author: Alistair Ryder

reviews.text: A ghost story drenched in gritty, saltwater-flecked period accuracy, and anchored in cautionary maritime fables, but one with a boozy, amorous, and darkly comic edge.
reviews.author: Rory O'Connor

reviews.text: Eggers confirms his instant reputation as a master of the New England Gothic with this claustrophobic second feature.
reviews.author: David Rooney

reviews.text: Shot in an expressionist black and white that harks back to cinema's earliest years, The Lighthouse provides a marvellous chamber-drama platform for two actors, Robert Pattinson and Willem Dafoe, who seize the opportunity with gusto.
reviews.author: Lee Marshall

reviews.text: It's the best movie about bad roommates ever made.
reviews.author: Eric Kohn

reviews.text: Very few films can make you scared and excited at the same time. Just like the lighthouse beam, this is dazzling and dangerous.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: "The Lighthouse," made with extraordinary skill, is a movie you can't pigeonhole, and that's part of its appeal.
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

synopsis: Two lighthouse keepers try to maintain their sanity while living on a remote and mysterious New England island in the 1890s.
